take_homes: An agent grading its own work goes easy on it, so use a fresh critic with only the artifact and ask for the generic bits first.
The chat summary is not the artifact. The rules file is what travels, and it needs a retro pass after each use.
The anti-branding flip works: list what annoys you, invert it, and use that as the spine. Also naming a famous site sets a style fast.

monday.move: Add a cold-critic step to the review flow of the sales-team setup: a fresh agent that sees only the output, asked for the generic or wrong parts first. Maybe. It depends on whether I stay interested.
monday.who: me, then probably one of my engineers
monday.when: midweek, if I get to it
monday.stop_condition: The critic flags nothing useful on two runs in a row, and then I drop it.
monday.blocker: Nobody outside engineering asked for the sales setup and I haven't checked who maintains it. I'll probably keep building before I add the check.

misconception.why: The point that agents grade their own work kindly is a failure mode I hadn't met. I still think checking is mostly for beginners. But I'd have waved off the review steps as ceremony, and that slide made it concrete.

one_line: Two or three good ideas on self-review bias and rules files, buried under fourteen copies of the same filler slide, and it's paced for people who've never seen an agent.
